newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOY SHIPPING CONDITIONS AT KEY BRAZILIAN PORTS.
newsitem.headline: SOY SHIPPING CONDITIONS AT KEY BRAZILIAN PORTS.

text.p: The Brazilian ports of Paranagua and Santos reported the following conditions for shipping soybeans and soy products:

Vessels: Nadelhorn loading 25,612 tonnes soymeal. Major Hubal loading 30,921 tonnes soymeal. Peljesac loading 55,000 tonnes soymeal. Waiting to dock, six vessels to load soymeal, five to load soybeans and two for mixed cargo (soybeans/meal). Road: 461 trucks carrying soybeans arrived on Aug 5, as well as 112 trucks with soymeal and 79 trucks with vegetable oils, including soyoil.

Loading: In July, the port loaded 606,215 tonnes soybeans, 638,558 tonnes soymeal and 120,550 tonnes vegetable oils, including soyoil. In July 1996, it loaded 197,129 tonnes soybeans, 666,450 tonnes soymeal and 142,123 tonnes vegetable oils, including soyoil.
NOTE: Light rain was delaying the loading of grains at the port since Monday.
Vessels: Captain Diamantis loading 22,000 tonnes soybeans.

Waiting to dock, two vessels to load soybeans. At Cutrale terminal, Gardno loading 15,000 tonnes soymeal. At Cargill private terminal, Lika loading 60,000 tonnes soymeal. Waiting to dock, one vessel to load 57,500 tonnes soymeal.
Road: 20 trucks carrying 506 tonnes soybeans arrived on Aug 5 as well as 24 trucks with 652 tonnes soymeal.
Rail: four wagons arrived carrying 238 tonnes soymeal.
NOTE: Early rains dissipated leaving clear skies over the port.
